messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: BIIIG occupancy model with occu()
parts:
Dear Ken,

I am playing around with the new spOccupancy package to fit spatial occupancy models to big data sets and wanted to compare an analysis with unmarked. It's a static occupancy model with 21,000 sites, 14 occasions and mostly NA's and zeroes (it's for a rare species). I fit a model with two continuous obs covs in detection and 34 (!) continuous site covs in occupancy. Surprisingly I get convergence in unmarked in less than 10 minutes (as opposed to 5 hours in spOccupancy).

However, I get this warning:
Warning message:
Using formula(x) is deprecated when x is a character vector of length > 1.
  Consider formula(paste(x, collapse = " ")) instead.

What does that mean ?

Just for curiosity I attach a plot that compares the MLEs produced by unmarked with the posterior means from spOccupancy. They do match for the most part, but we see that MLE is susceptible to problems with boundary estimates (I believe). Providing solutions from spOccupancy for inits in unmarked helps, but does not avoid this entirely.

Thanks and best regards  ---- Marc

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: BIIIG occupancy model with occu()
parts:
Hi Marc,

The warning is the result of a bug in the CRAN version (fixed in dev version) which appears when the formula is very long, as it likely is in your case. If you don't have random effects in the model you can safely ignore the warning.

Thanks for sending the spOccupancy comparison as well - I need to take a closer look at the package, it seems very cool.

Ken
